newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Deutsche Bank issues Fletcher Challenge warrants.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank issues Fletcher Challenge warrants.

text.p: Deutsche Bank said on Friday it was issuing separate call warrants over each of the four listed Fletcher Challenge stocks.

The warrants, expiring on April 22, 1999, allow investors to buy one share in the specified letter stock for every two warrants exercised. The initial public offer opens on March 10 and the warrants will trade on the New Zealand Stock Exchange from March 17.
The exercise prices per share are:
Fletcher Challenge Energy NZ$4.50 per share;
Deutsche said this followed the successful launch in early February of Telecom call warrants.
The issue price for the four FCL warrants will vary depending on the performance of the underlying shares.
"They will be issued at a fraction of the underlying share price, proving a leveraged exposure to the Fletcher Challenge letter stocks," it said.
"There is clearly demand for an instrument which is both liquid and gives investors leverage with limited risk."
Warrant holders have the right but not the obligation to buy FCL letter shares at any time before the expiry. Brokers to the issue are Garlick and Co.
